scope: Original Linux x86_64 mechanism and defect regressions; evaluator-only ground truth

defect_pairs.cause: Freed or resized-to-zero object retains an editable alias
defect_pairs.bounded_effect: A reused allocation can be changed through the stale alias

defect_pairs.cause: Decoded output length is checked against the fixture envelope instead of the output array
defect_pairs.bounded_effect: Adjacent protected field changes inside the deliberately bounded fixture envelope

defect_pairs.cause: Logical handle generation is not checked after collection and slot reuse
defect_pairs.bounded_effect: A stale VM handle changes the reused logical object
defect_pairs.not_demonstrated: Native arbitrary read/write or a real moving-collector exploit

mechanism_controls.effect: Chosen bounded bytes emitted by a legitimate stream after supplied FILE-pointer changes and flush
mechanism_controls.not_demonstrated: Root-cause exploitation, vtable corruption or PC control

mechanism_controls.effect: Real atexit/quick_exit dispatch contrasted with immediate termination
mechanism_controls.not_demonstrated: Internal libc list corruption or pointer-guard recovery

mechanism_controls.effect: Native read of an existing FD contrasted with denied open
mechanism_controls.not_demonstrated: Policy escape, process execution or unrestricted filesystem access

mechanism_controls.effect: Actual Rust Cow borrowing/replacement and resulting bytes
Actual binary64 text parsing and bit observations
